task: A colleague suggests doing an upgrade at the weekend. You agree. Say so and give a reason.
say: I think we should do the upgrade on a Saturday, when it's quiet.
zh: 同事建议周末做升级。你同意。表示赞同并给出理由。对方说：我觉得升级应该放在周六做，那时候人少。
example: Yeah, I agree. Saturday makes sense, since fewer people will be affected.

task: Your manager has a big idea. You like the idea but not the timing. Agree with part of it.
say: Let's move all our servers to the cloud this year.
zh: 经理提了一个大计划。你喜欢这个想法，但不认同时间安排。部分同意。对方说：我们今年把所有服务器都搬到云上吧。
example: I like the idea, but I'm not sure about this year. It might be better to do it in stages.

task: A colleague wants to skip testing. Disagree politely and say why.
say: We don't need to test this. It's only a small change.
zh: 同事想跳过测试。礼貌地表示不同意，并说明原因。对方说：这个不用测了，只是个小改动。
example: I'm not sure about that. Even small changes can break things, so I'd still do a quick test.

task: Your manager asks for a report by tomorrow. That's not possible. Say no politely and offer another day.
say: Can you have the report ready by tomorrow?
zh: 经理要你明天交报告，但做不到。礼貌地拒绝，并提出另一个时间。对方说：报告明天能准备好吗？
example: Tomorrow's going to be tough, sorry. I could have it ready by Thursday morning. Would that work?

task: Someone suggests something risky for security. Raise your concern.
say: Let's give everyone admin rights so they can install what they need.
zh: 有人提了一个有安全风险的建议。说出你的担心。对方说：干脆给每个人管理员权限吧，这样他们需要什么就能自己装。
example: I'm a bit worried about that. If everyone's an admin, it's much easier for malware to spread.

task: A colleague makes a good suggestion in a team meeting. Show your support and add a reason.
say: I think we should get the service desk involved earlier.
zh: 同事在团队会上提了一个好建议。表示支持并补充一个理由。对方说：我觉得应该早点让服务台参与进来。
example: Good idea. They hear what users are complaining about every day, so they'd give us really useful feedback.

task: A colleague suggests a quick fix that hides the real problem. Accept it for now, but offer a better long-term option.
say: Let's just restart the server every night to fix the memory leak.
zh: 同事提了一个治标不治本的快速办法。暂时接受，但提出一个更好的长期方案。对方说：我们每晚重启一次服务器，解决内存泄漏就行了。
example: That would work short term. How about we also log a ticket with the vendor? Then we can fix the real problem.

words.en: get to the root of it

task: A client asks for extra work that isn't in the project. Say no politely and offer another way.
say: While you're at it, could you also set up our Teams phone system?
zh: 客户要求做一些不在项目范围内的额外工作。礼貌地拒绝，并给出另一种办法。对方说：你们顺便把我们的 Teams 电话系统也配一下吧？
example: That's not part of this project, unfortunately. But I'm happy to get you a separate quote for it.

words.zh: 让这个项目按计划进行

task: The project manager wants to cut testing time in half. Stand your ground and give a reason from experience.
say: Do we really need two weeks for testing? Can't you do it in one?
zh: 项目经理想把测试时间砍掉一半。坚持你的立场，用过去的经验说明理由。对方说：测试真的需要两周吗？一周不行吗？
example: I'd really recommend two weeks. Last time we rushed testing, we found bugs after go-live, and fixing them took even longer.

task: A senior colleague wants to skip the backup before an upgrade. Disagree respectfully.
say: I reckon we skip the backup before the upgrade. It takes too long.
zh: 一位资深同事想在升级前跳过备份。尊重地表示反对。对方说：我觉得升级前就别备份了，太花时间。
example: I see your point, but I'd feel much better with a backup. If the upgrade fails, we'd have nothing to roll back to.

task: A colleague says a technology will be cheaper. That's only partly true. Agree with part, then add a 'but'.
say: Serverless will definitely be cheaper for us.
zh: 同事说某项技术会更便宜。这只说对了一部分。先认同一部分，再用 but 补充。对方说：用无服务器肯定会更便宜。
example: That's true for small workloads. But with our traffic, it might end up costing more. Could we run the numbers first?

task: Your manager wants to give you another regular task, but you're already too busy. Push back politely and suggest a later time.
say: Can you also take over the backup checks from next week?
zh: 经理想再给你加一项日常工作，但你已经忙不过来了。礼貌地推辞，并建议以后再说。对方说：从下周开始，备份检查也交给你吧？
example: I'd like to help, but I'm flat out with the migration until the end of the month. Could we look at it again in December?

task: A colleague proposes letting staff use their own phones for work email. Agree, but add a condition.
say: Let's let people use their own phones for work email.
zh: 同事提议让员工用自己的手机收工作邮件。表示同意，但加一个前提条件。对方说：让大家用自己的手机收工作邮件吧。
example: I'm fine with that, as long as we set up Intune policies first, so we can wipe company data if a phone gets lost.

task: Everyone seems to agree, but you have a doubt. Offer a different view politely.
say: So we all agree to keep the vendor's default settings?
zh: 大家似乎都同意了，但你有疑问。礼貌地提出不同看法。对方说：那我们都同意保留供应商的默认设置？
example: Can I play devil's advocate for a sec? Some of the defaults aren't great for security, so I think we should review them first.

words.en: just to throw it out there

task: A stakeholder wants you to start building with no clear requirements. Push back and explain the risk.
say: Just start building and we'll figure out the details later.
zh: 一位相关方让你在需求不清楚的情况下就开始开发。提出异议并解释风险。对方说：先开始做吧，细节以后再说。
example: I'd rather not start without the main requirements. If we change direction later, we'll throw away a lot of work.

task: A client pushes for a deadline that isn't realistic. Show you understand, say no honestly, and offer an alternative.
say: We really need this live before Christmas. Can you make it happen?
zh: 客户坚持一个不现实的截止日期。表示理解，坦诚拒绝，再给出替代方案。对方说：我们真的需要在圣诞节前上线。你们能做到吗？
example: I understand why Christmas matters. Honestly, the full system isn't realistic by then. What we could do is launch the core features first and add the rest in January.

task: A manager challenges your recommendation a second time. Stand your ground calmly and offer to show the evidence.
say: I still think we could manage without the extra licences.
zh: 一位经理第二次质疑你的建议。冷静地坚持立场，并提出可以展示依据。对方说：我还是觉得不用多买那些许可证也行。
example: I've looked at it closely, and I don't think we can. Without them, we'd lose conditional access, which is a key security control. I'm happy to walk you through the details.

task: In a design review, an architect suggests a design you think won't scale. Disagree, give your option, and suggest comparing.
say: Let's put everything in one big virtual network. It's simpler that way.
zh: 设计评审会上，一位架构师提出一个你认为扩展性不好的设计。表示不同意，提出你的方案，并建议对比一下。对方说：所有东西放进一个大的虚拟网络里吧，这样简单。
example: It's simpler to start with, I agree. But a hub-and-spoke design would give us better control as we grow. Could we compare the two?

task: In a sprint review, someone criticises your dashboard quite rudely. Stay calm, accept the fair part, and move to a solution.
say: This dashboard is way too complicated. Who designed it?
zh: 迭代评审会上，有人很不客气地批评你做的仪表板。保持冷静，接受合理的部分，再转向解决办法。对方说：这个仪表板太复杂了。谁设计的？
example: Fair enough, it is quite busy. We built it from the original wish list, but I'm happy to simplify it. Which parts do you actually use?

task: Someone wants to save money in a way that creates risk. Recognise the saving, explain the catch, and suggest a middle option.
say: Let's turn off the test environment to save money.
zh: 有人想省钱，但这样做会带来风险。先肯定能省钱，再指出问题，然后提出折中方案。对方说：把测试环境关掉省点钱吧。
example: We'd save about two thousand a month, which is great. The catch is we'd have nowhere to test patches. Could we just shut it down at night and at weekends instead?

task: A vendor promises their product will just work. You're not convinced. Push back politely and ask for proof.
say: Our product will work with your setup out of the box. No changes needed.
zh: 供应商保证他们的产品开箱即用。你不太相信。礼貌地提出质疑，要求证明。对方说：我们的产品可以直接适配你们的环境，不需要任何改动。
example: That would be great. Our setup's a bit unusual, though, so I'd like to see it working in a proof of concept before we commit.

task: At a steering meeting, everyone is about to approve a risky cutover plan. Raise your concern and suggest a safer way.
say: So we're happy to cut over all three sites on the same day?
zh: 在指导委员会会议上，大家准备批准一个有风险的切换计划。提出你的顾虑，并建议更安全的做法。对方说：那我们同意三个站点同一天切换？
example: I have some concerns about that. If something goes wrong, all three sites are down at once. I'd suggest doing one site first as a pilot.

words.en: all our eggs in one basket

task: Your manager wants you to promise a client something you can't deliver. Refuse respectfully and suggest an honest answer.
say: Just tell them yes for now. We'll sort it out later.
zh: 经理让你向客户承诺一件做不到的事。尊重但坚定地拒绝，并建议一个诚实的回答。对方说：先答应他们吧，以后再想办法。
example: I'm not comfortable promising that. If we miss it, we lose their trust. How about I tell them we'll confirm the date once the design is signed off?

task: The client's IT manager says, in front of their team, that admin accounts don't need MFA. Disagree respectfully without embarrassing them.
say: We don't need MFA on the admin accounts. Our people are careful.
zh: 客户的 IT 经理当着团队的面说管理员账户不需要多因素认证。尊重地表示反对，不要让对方难堪。对方说：管理员账户不需要 MFA，我们的人都很小心。
example: I don't doubt your team at all. The risk is more about stolen passwords, which can happen to anyone. MFA on admin accounts is one of the cheapest ways to protect you.

task: A product owner keeps pushing to add work to a full sprint. Stay friendly, hold firm, and make them choose.
say: Come on, it's only a small change. Can't you just squeeze it in this sprint?
zh: 产品负责人一直要求往已经排满的迭代里加任务。保持友好、坚持立场，让对方做取舍。对方说：拜托，就一个小改动。这个迭代挤一挤加进去不行吗？
example: I get it, and it does look small. But the sprint's already full, so adding it means something else slips. If it's urgent, which item would you like to swap out?
